kurzbeschreibung: The Stubai Valley charms visitors with the Stubai Glacier, Austria's largest glacier ski area, roaring waterfalls along the Wild Water Trail, and breathtaking peaks.
beschreibung: The Stubai Valley (Stubaital) lies just 20 minutes south of Innsbruck and is one of Tyrol's most striking alpine valleys. The five municipalities of Schönberg, Mieders, Telfes, Fulpmes, and Neustift combine deep-rooted traditions with premier outdoor experiences. Crowned by the massive Stubai Glacier—Austria's largest glacier ski resort with snow reliability from October to May and the Top of Tyrol (3,210 m) viewpoint—the region also features the iconic Zuckerhütl (3,507 m) and the 'Seven Summits Stubai'. The Stubai High Trail (Stubaier Höhenweg) is renowned as one of the finest hut-to-hut circuits in the Alps.
tipps: Marvel at Grawa Waterfall along the Wild Water Trail – at 85 m wide, it is the broadest waterfall in the Eastern Alps.
Explore the Blacksmith Museum in Fulpmes showcasing centuries of world-famous Tyrolean iron craftsmanship.
Ride the historic scenic Stubaitalbahn light rail train directly from Innsbruck through alpine meadows to Fulpmes.
empfehlungen: Take the 3S Eisgrat cable car up to the Stubai Glacier to tour the walk-in ice cave and take in panoramic vistas from Top of Tyrol. For lunch, dine at the award-winning Schaufelspitz Restaurant (2,900 m) or enjoy fresh trout at rustic Tschangelair Alm.
umgebung: The Stubai Valley branches off westwards from the Wipptal at Schönberg. It borders the Innsbruck region and Sellrain Valley to the north, the Ötztal Valley to the west, Wipptal to the east, and South Tyrol (Italy) along the main Alpine ridge to the south.
